title: Reading Controlled SOPs and Work Orders

content.overview: Technician I workers must identify the current controlled instruction, reconcile it with the specific work order, and recognize acceptance criteria, exceptions and escalation points before acting.

vocabulary.definition: A controlled standard operating procedure describing how an activity is performed within its defined scope.
An instruction assigning a specific task, location, material, timing or quantity under a controlled procedure.
Defined conditions that indicate whether a step, result or completed task meets requirements.

sections.title: Use the current instruction
sections.body: A technician verifies the current approved SOP, work order or digital instruction supplied by the facility. Memory does not replace the controlled version when the task is governed by one.

sections.title: Reconcile procedure and assignment
sections.body: The SOP defines the standard method while the work order applies it to a specific room, batch, quantity or shift. A conflict between the two, or between the instructions and actual conditions, is escalated rather than resolved by choosing the more convenient instruction.

workedExamples: An older printed SOP is found beside a current controlled digital revision; the technician follows document-control procedure before working.
A room assignment conflicts with the listed batch identifier, so movement pauses until the mismatch is resolved.
commonMistakes: Following an obsolete procedure because it is familiar.
Ignoring acceptance criteria once the physical task appears complete.
content.practicalApplication: Review a mock SOP and work order, identify prerequisites, steps, acceptance criteria, required records and escalation points, and flag a planted revision conflict.
content.summary: Controlled work begins with the right instruction. Technicians verify current procedures, reconcile the assignment and escalate conflicts rather than improvising.

blocks.title: Read the instruction as a controlled object
blocks.body: Before acting, verify which instruction governs the task and whether it is the current controlled version. A familiar printed page, remembered routine, screenshot, or locally saved copy can be obsolete even when it looks official. The technician uses the facility's document-control process rather than choosing the version that is easiest to reach.

blocks.alt: Annotated controlled SOP showing document identity and revision, scope and prerequisites, material or asset identity, step sequence, acceptance criteria, required records, and escalation points, beside a work-order card containing the specific room, batch, asset, quantity, date, and shift context.
blocks.caption: The SOP defines the controlled method; the work order applies that method to specific work. A conflict must be resolved, not guessed away.

blocks.title: Five checks before controlled work begins

items.title: Verify document control
items.body: Confirm the instruction ID, revision or effective status, and the facility's indication that the version is current.

items.title: Check scope and prerequisites
items.body: Confirm the task is within the instruction's scope and that required training, PPE, tools, setup, or authorization are present.

items.title: Reconcile the work order
items.body: Match the room, material, batch, asset, quantity, date, shift, or other specific assignment details to physical reality.

items.title: Find acceptance criteria and records
items.body: Know what proves the work is complete and which observations, measurements, identities, times, or signoffs must be recorded.

items.title: Find decision and escalation points
items.body: Know which conditions change, stop, or transfer the task before you reach them in the workflow.

blocks.title: The binder copy and the controlled digital copy disagree
blocks.setting: A printed SOP in the grow room says Revision 4. The controlled document system shows Revision 6 as effective. Revision 6 changed one verification step. A coworker says the binder copy is what everyone uses.
blocks.prompt: What is the strongest Technician I response?
options: Use Revision 4 because it is physically located in the room
Use whichever version has the faster workflow
Follow the facility's document-control process and use the confirmed current instruction before affected work
Combine the steps from both versions
blocks.answer: Follow the facility's document-control process and use the confirmed current instruction before affected work.
blocks.feedback: Familiarity and physical location do not establish document status. A controlled process should identify the current authorized version and address obsolete copies.

blocks.title: Controlled-instruction review card
blocks.description: A short pre-task review should make the instruction and assignment testable instead of relying on memory.

fields.label: Task scope
fields.value: What activity, area, asset, or material the instruction covers

fields.label: Prerequisites
fields.value: Training, PPE, setup, tools, or authorization needed before starting

fields.label: Work-order identifiers
fields.value: Room, batch/material, asset, quantity, date/shift, or other assigned context

fields.label: Required records
fields.value: Measurements, identities, times, observations, or signoffs that must be captured

fields.label: Stop / escalation points
fields.value: Conditions that require clarification, approval, hold, stop-work, or referral

blocks.note: A mismatch between the instruction, work order, and physical situation remains an open issue until the authorized process resolves it.

blocks.title: Audit a mock SOP and work order
blocks.instructions: Review a supplied controlled procedure and work order containing one obsolete revision cue, one identity mismatch, and one overlooked acceptance criterion.
prompts: Identify the evidence that establishes the current instruction.
List the work-order details that must match physical reality.
Find the planted conflict and explain why the technician should not choose a convenient interpretation.
Identify the acceptance criterion that proves completion.
Identify the record fields and escalation point needed before closeout.

blocks.title: Key takeaway
blocks.body: Controlled work starts before the physical task. Verify the current instruction, reconcile the specific assignment, understand what success looks like, and surface conflicts while there is still time to resolve them correctly.
